text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Charges for driving on two Singapore expressways at peak hours will be introduced from May 5 and 5,500 more Certificates of Entitlement for car users will be issued as the congestion eases. Road tax rebates of about Singapore $36.0 million will be made, the Minister of Communications said.
- All industrial tenants of Housing Development Board (HDB) properties will be relocated over the next 10 years in a S$5.0 billion upgrading scheme, the National Development Ministry said.
- About S$125.0 million will be spent over 10 years in a new scholarship programme to groom Singapore's future business leaders, Trade and Industry Minister Lee Yock Suan said.
- Recovery in the Singapore economy is expected to happen this year but its pace and timing are still uncertain, Minister for Trade and Industry Lee Yock Suan said.
- A S$165.0 million bid by Straits Steamship Land places it as the frontrunner in the purchase of Singapore's Avenue Park development, one of the largest sites on the island.
- Nusamba group, owned by foundations controlled by President Suharto, aims to turn itself into Indonesia's answer to the Rockefeller Foundation, Nusamba's chief said.

- Stock analysts said they welcomed government plans to increase the number of Certificates of Entitlement for Singapore motorists and expected positive effects for listed motor dealers and importers.
- Turnover of foreign currency stocks listed in Singapore jumped 30 percent in 1996 to S$8.96 billion from S$6.93 billion a year previously, the Stock Exchange of Singapore said.
- Insider trading does not sully Singapore's corporations and investors do not necessarily favour stocks bought by insiders, a study by the Stock Exchange of Singapore said.
- Malaysian newspaper group, the New Straits Times Press, is proposing a S$40.0 million investment in a new South African newspaper, according to a report in South Africa's weekly Financial Mail.
- Instant coffee maker Super Coffeemix Manufacturing plans to raise S$26.0 million through the issue of 20 million new shares, the company said.
